ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.summary: Neither library has complex multiplication. Mathlib supplies the ambient field theory a CM development would sit on — `NumberField.IsCMField` with the maximal real subfield and complex conjugation, the idele group and idele class group, class groups and Dedekind-domain ideal theory, `WeierstrassCurve.j` with `exists_variableChange_of_j_eq`, and integral models/good-and-bad reduction; Tau Ceti supplies ideal-theoretic ray class groups with a modulus, the Artin symbol at unramified primes with Chebotarev, and a substantial elliptic-curve isogeny theory (the Hom group, degree multiplicativity, kernels, separability, Frobenius factorisation). Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap names: CM types and reflex norms, orders of a number field other than the maximal one (so no proper invertible ideals, no conductor, no ring class group), the analytic uniformization ℓattice → elliptic curve, the main theorem of complex multiplication, class polynomials, ring and ray class *fields* as fields, algebraic Hecke characters, Tate modules, abelian varieties and the Shimura–Taniyama formula. The roadmap's own targets are therefore almost entirely unbuilt; its CM.2 is by construction a re-export of ShimuraVarieties:V5, which is itself unbuilt.

targets.target: Orders in CM fields (subrings of finite index in the ring of integers) and their conductors
targets.note: Mathlib defines a CM field (totally complex quadratic over its maximal totally real subfield) and its complex conjugation, but has no notion of an order: only the maximal order `𝓞 K` exists. `grep -rn 'an order in|non-maximal order|order of conductor'` over both libraries returns nothing in this sense, and the only `conductor` declarations are `DirichletCharacter.conductor` and a `Subalgebra`-conductor lemma for quadratic splitting.

targets.target: Proper invertible ideals of an order and the ideal class group of an order, distinguished from the class group of the maximal order
targets.note: Mathlib's `ClassGroup R` is the Picard group of fractional ideals of a Dedekind domain, so it is only the class group of the *maximal* order; Tau Ceti's ray class groups are quotients of ideals prime to a modulus inside `𝓞 K`. Proper (= with multiplier ring exactly the order) invertible ideals of a non-maximal order, and their class group, exist nowhere.

targets.target: CM types Φ ⊂ Hom(K,ℂ) with Φ ⊔ Φ̄ = Hom(K,ℂ), and non-Galois CM types
targets.note: The two ingredients (complex embeddings and their conjugation, complex conjugation on a CM field) are in Mathlib, but no set-of-embeddings structure with the CM-type condition is defined; `grep -rn -i 'CM type'` over both libraries returns nothing.

targets.target: The reflex field and reflex norm of a CM type, on the existing torus/idele objects
targets.note: The idele group and idele class group of a number field are in Mathlib, and the field norm is there, but no reflex field and no reflex norm N_Φ is defined in either library. `grep -rn -i 'reflex'` returns nothing.

targets.target: Conjugation and change-of-type formulas for CM types
targets.note: Depends on the CM-type definition, which does not exist.

duplicates.note: V5 explicitly says 'Construct CM types, reflex types, reflex norms, and the Tate-module action', which is the whole of CM.0 in greater generality.
M0 constructs the field of definition of the determinant condition and identifies it with the reflex field, overlapping CM.0's reflex-field target.
D3 defines the conjugacy class {µ}, its Galois action and the reflex field as the fixed field of its stabiliser — the reflex field of CM.0 is the special case of a CM torus.

targets.target: The elliptic curve ℂ/𝔞 attached to a complex lattice / ideal of an order, with its order action
targets.note: Elliptic curves exist only as Weierstrass equations; there is no Weierstrass ℘-function, no Eisenstein series g₂/g₃ of a lattice, and no uniformization ℂ/Λ ≅ E(ℂ). Tau Ceti's `ComplexTorus` is the algebraic torus (ℂˣ)ⁿ of toric geometry, not ℂ/Λ.

targets.target: Identification of isomorphism classes of such curves with proper ideal classes of the order
targets.note: Mathlib proves that equal j-invariants give isomorphic curves over an algebraically closed field, which is the classification input; the bijection with proper ideal classes needs both the lattice construction and the order class group, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Automorphism factors at j = 0 and j = 1728 (extra automorphisms of the curve)
targets.note: Tau Ceti computes the automorphism group of a Weierstrass curve as a group of variable changes, with the j = 0 and j = 1728 characterisations available; this is the only target of this layer with library support, and it is stated for Weierstrass models rather than for lattices.

targets.target: Action of an invertible prime ideal on the curve and its isogeny degree
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a genuine isogeny theory — `Hom(W₁,W₂)` as an additive group, multiplicative degree, kernels, separability and Frobenius factorisation — so the target of an ideal action (an isogeny of prescribed degree) has a home. The action of an ideal itself is absent, since it needs the order and the lattice model.

targets.target: Comparison of analytic and algebraic endomorphism rings
targets.note: The algebraic side (End as a ring with no zero divisors, degree multiplicative) is built in Tau Ceti; the analytic side (End(ℂ/Λ) = {α : αΛ ⊆ Λ}) does not exist, so the comparison cannot even be stated. No theorem identifying End with an order in an imaginary quadratic field is present.

duplicates.note: HE.1 constructs CM elliptic curves and cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ and descends them to ring class fields — the same complex CM curves and ideal actions as CM.1, used for Heegner points.
A5 proves the Riemann bilinear relations and algebraicity of polarized complex tori, the general form of the analytic-quotient-equals-algebraic-curve comparison CM.1 asks for in dimension one.

targets.target: The main theorem of complex multiplication (the reciprocity law for the Galois action on a CM abelian variety and its torsion)
targets.note: Nothing towards this exists: there are no abelian varieties, no Tate modules (`grep -i tateModule` is empty), and no CM types in either library. The layer is itself framed as importing ShimuraVarieties:V5, which is unbuilt.

targets.target: Ideal, idele and torsion-level dictionaries with a fixed Artin convention
targets.note: Tau Ceti fixes the arithmetic Artin convention at unramified primes (conjugacy-class valued, with functoriality in towers) and has ideal-theoretic ray class groups; Mathlib has the idele class group. The ideal ↔ idele comparison itself — the global reciprocity map — is not proved in either library; Tau Ceti's `ClassFieldTheory/Formation` is the abstract class-formation machinery only, with no arithmetic instance.

targets.target: Separation of base field, CM endomorphism field and reflex field
targets.note: All three notions presuppose CM types and reflex norms, which are absent.

targets.target: Action on torsion and polarizations in a dimension-two example
targets.note: No abelian surfaces, polarizations or torsion-level structures exist in either library.

duplicates.note: V5 states 'Prove the main theorem of complex multiplication' including the Shimura–Taniyama Frobenius calculation and the passage to the full reciprocity law; CM.2 is by its own text a re-import and comparison of exactly that theorem.
V7 handles conjugation and descent for general Shimura data, which subsumes CM.2's Artin-convention bookkeeping for the CM case.

targets.target: The class polynomial H_D(X) = ∏_{[𝔞]} (X − j(𝔞)) over proper ideal classes
targets.note: The j-invariant of a Weierstrass curve exists, but the modular function j on the upper half plane does not (no `jFunction`, no Klein invariant; Mathlib's `UpperHalfPlane.J` is the symplectic matrix, not the modular function), so j(𝔞) for a lattice cannot be written and the product over ideal classes does not exist.

targets.target: Algebraic integrality of the j-values (H_D ∈ ℤ[X])
targets.note: Only the general integral-closure machinery is available; the integrality of singular moduli is not proved.

targets.target: Galois equivariance of the j-values and the identification of the ring class field of an order in an imaginary quadratic field
targets.note: No class field of any kind is constructed in either library: `grep -rn -i 'hilbert class field|ring class field|ray class field'` finds only a passing remark in a Tau Ceti docstring. Tau Ceti's ray class *groups* exist but no abelian extension is attached to them.

targets.target: Ray-class variants using level (modular) functions with admissibility conditions
targets.note: The ray subgroup of a modulus is defined in Tau Ceti; the Weber functions / level functions generating ray class fields are absent.

duplicates.note: HE.1 also proves descent of CM points to ring class fields, so the ring-class-field identification is stated twice.

targets.target: Algebraic Hecke characters attached to CM abelian varieties
targets.note: There is no Hecke character, Größencharakter or idele-class character anywhere: the only `Hecke` declarations in either library are the abstract Hecke ring and its GL₂ instances (Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing, TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing), which are double-coset algebras, not characters.

targets.target: Infinity type and finite conductor of such a character
targets.note: Only the conductor of a Dirichlet character (a character of (ℤ/n)ˣ) exists; there is no conductor of an idele class character and no infinity type.

targets.target: Frobenius identities ψ(𝔭) = a_𝔭 at good primes
targets.note: The Artin symbol and its Chebotarev equidistribution are available in Tau Ceti, but there is no L-series of an elliptic curve with proved Euler factors at good primes to match against; Mathlib's `EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean` is not a proved Euler product over the CM decomposition.

targets.target: Comparison of the one-dimensional components of the ℓ-adic representation with the Tate module; splitting of the rank-two representation for a CM curve
targets.note: No Tate module of an elliptic curve or abelian variety is defined in either library (`grep -i tateModule` is empty), so neither the rank-two representation nor its CM decomposition can be stated.

duplicates.note: V5's 'Tate-module action' for CM abelian varieties is the same object CM.4 compares its characters against.
L3 covers totally real abelian and CM constructions, which build on the same CM Hecke characters.

targets.target: The Shimura–Taniyama formula for the reduction of a CM abelian variety
targets.note: Absent; it presupposes CM types and reduction of abelian varieties, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Isogeny graphs of CM elliptic curves at a good prime; ordinary versus supersingular reduction
targets.note: Good/multiplicative/additive reduction classes and integral models are in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti has isogenies with degrees, kernels and the relative Frobenius; but there is no `IsSupersingular`/`IsOrdinary` predicate anywhere (`grep -i supersingular` is empty), so the dichotomy the acceptance clause turns on is not even expressible.

targets.target: Certified complex or CRT computation of class polynomials with proved height/precision bounds
targets.note: Class polynomials do not exist, and no certified-numerics framework for algebraic numbers with error certificates is present in either library.

targets.target: Endomorphism-ring verification as a separate certificate
targets.note: The endomorphism carrier exists in Tau Ceti but is not identified with an order in a quadratic field, and there is no algorithm or certificate for computing it.

duplicates.note: V5 lists 'reduction of CM abelian varieties at suitable primes, the Shimura–Taniyama Frobenius calculation' among its proof obligations, the same statement CM.5 instantiates.

targets.target: Export of ring/ray class fields, torsion fields, Hecke characters and ideal-action theorems to downstream applications
targets.note: This is an interface/re-export task over CM.0–CM.5, none of whose objects exist; it states no new mathematics of its own.

targets.target: Documentation of which level functions generate the asserted field
targets.note: Bookkeeping over the (absent) ray class field construction of CM.3.

targets.target: A worked elliptic ring-class example and a higher-dimensional reflex-field example
targets.note: Acceptance examples for the preceding layers; no independent target.

duplicates.note: The named consumer of CM.6's ring-class-field export already states the same descent to ring class fields as one of its own obligations.

EffectiveDiophantineMethods.summary: The libraries have the *mathematical* inputs to effective Diophantine work but none of its algorithmic content. Mathlib supplies the Weil height machine with the Northcott finiteness theorem, Minkowski's convex-body theorem and ℤ-lattices, the p-adics with their valuation, and Liouville/continued-fraction Diophantine approximation; Tau Ceti supplies the Mordell–Weil theorem over a number field, a genuine 2-Selmer group cut out by local conditions at every finite place with the rank bound 2^r · #E(K)[2] ≤ #S, the Néron–Tate canonical height with its parallelogram law, and Riemann–Roch with the genus for function fields. Genuinely missing is every effective and certified ingredient the roadmap is about: LLL and any lattice reduction with proved approximation factor, interval/ball arithmetic and root isolation for algebraic numbers, Baker–Matveev linear forms in logarithms (archimedean or p-adic), S-unit and Thue–Mahler theory, p-adic logarithms and exponentials, rigid cohomology and Coleman integration, Chabauty's theorem, the Mordell–Weil sieve and saturation. ED.0–ED.2 are also framed as imports from ComputationalNumberTheory and GeometryOfNumbers rather than new mathematics.

targets.target: Certified exact presentations of algebraic numbers (isolating intervals and discs, with proved separation)
targets.note: Minimal polynomials and root multisets exist, but no root-isolation procedure, Sturm sequence, separation bound or interval presentation of an algebraic number is present in either library; `grep -i 'isolating|Sturm'` finds only Sturm bounds for modular forms, an unrelated notion.

targets.target: Local (p-adic) precision models and valuation adapters
targets.note: The mathematical carriers — p-adic numbers with their valuation, adic valuations and completions of a Dedekind domain — are complete in Mathlib. What is missing is a *precision model*: truncation to a finite p-adic precision with a proved error relation to the exact value.

targets.target: Rational error bounds attached to every approximate output, checked independently
targets.note: No interval or ball arithmetic exists in either library (`grep -i 'IntervalArith|BallArith|errorBound'` is empty), so there is no carrier on which a certified approximation could be stated.

duplicates.note: CN.0 specifies exact integers, rationals, algebraic numbers, finite fields, ideals, lattices and p-adic approximations with their complexity model; ED.0 says it imports exactly these and adds adapters.
CN.4 constructs interval/ball arithmetic, precision propagation and certified roots — the same certified-numerics layer, which ED.0's error-bound acceptance clause restates.

targets.target: LLL lattice reduction with exact Gram–Schmidt arithmetic, termination and a proved approximation factor
targets.note: Gram–Schmidt over a real or complex inner product space and ℤ-lattices with fundamental domains are in Mathlib, but there is no LLL algorithm, no size-reduced/Lovász-condition basis, no termination proof and no 2^{(n-1)/2} approximation bound anywhere (`grep -i LLL` over both libraries finds nothing relevant).

targets.target: Short-vector certificates: a proved lower bound on ‖v‖ over all nonzero lattice vectors in a region
targets.note: Minkowski's convex-body theorem gives an *upper* bound on the shortest vector and is fully proved; the layer needs the opposite direction — a certified lower bound excluding all integer vectors in a box, which is what LLL supplies and which is absent.

targets.target: Closest-vector certificates
targets.note: No CVP formulation or certificate exists in either library.

duplicates.note: GN.5 supplies 'LLL-style reduction ... with exact change-of-basis certificates' and the checked short-vector output; ED.1 states it imports this and adds a Diophantine adapter, so the LLL target is owned there.

targets.target: Explicit archimedean lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms (Baker–Matveev) with their constants and degree/height dependence
targets.note: Mathlib has Liouville's inequality and the transcendence of Liouville numbers, but no Baker-type bound and no Lindemann–Weierstrass or Gelfond–Schneider theorem; `grep -i 'Baker|Matveev'` over both libraries is empty.

targets.target: p-adic logarithms and explicit p-adic bounds for linear forms
targets.note: There is no p-adic logarithm or exponential in either library, so no p-adic form of the bound can be stated.

targets.target: S-unit equations x + y = 1 in S-units, and their finiteness/effective solution
targets.note: Dirichlet's unit theorem and the unit rank are in Mathlib, but the S-unit group, the S-unit equation and its finiteness are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Thue and Thue–Mahler equations with an enumerated solution box and a proof that every solution lies in it
targets.note: Absent; `grep -i Thue` over both libraries finds nothing.

targets.target: Certified evaluation of logarithms with propagated error
targets.note: The real logarithm and its analytic theory are complete in Mathlib; certified numerical evaluation with a rational enclosure is not present.

duplicates.note: DT.3 owns 'Baker-type explicit lower bounds, with chosen complex or p-adic logarithms' with the same degree/height/prime dependence clause; ED.2 imports it.
CN.4 owns the certified logarithm/error evaluation ED.2 consumes.

targets.target: Descent via 2-isogeny / the x−T map, and the Selmer group as a finite object
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the 2-Selmer group as the square classes in the étale algebra with trivial norm satisfying the local condition at every finite place of a Dedekind base and at an auxiliary family of completions, proves the descent map lands in it, and proves an auxiliary version finite. This is the classical 2-descent, proved sorry-free; it is a mathematical object, not an algorithm.

targets.target: Rank upper bound from the Selmer group
targets.note: `2 ^ rank E(K) · #E(K)[2] ≤ #S` for any finite S containing the image of the descent map is proved, on top of the Mordell–Weil theorem over any number field. This is the upper bound the layer asks for; only its *effective computation* is missing.

targets.target: Certified computation of the local images at each place
targets.note: The local conditions are defined and the set of bad primes is proved finite, so the Selmer group is cut out by finitely many nontrivial conditions; there is no procedure computing the local image as an explicit finite subgroup with a certificate.

targets.target: Saturation of a proposed Mordell–Weil subgroup at the required primes, and the matching lower bound on the rank
targets.note: The canonical height and the regulator of a set of points exist in Tau Ceti, which is the input a saturation argument needs; saturation itself — that a subgroup of finite index p is or is not p-saturated — is not formulated anywhere.

targets.target: A genus-one curve with a nontrivial torsor class (a 2-covering representing a nonzero Sha element)
targets.note: No Sha, no torsors under an elliptic curve and no genus-one models are constructed; the Selmer group exists but its quotient by the image of descent is never identified with Sha[2].

duplicates.note: RP.1 is the declared supplier: it states weak Mordell–Weil and descent, so the Selmer group and rank bound are stated in both places.

targets.target: Smooth proper genus-g curve over ℚ with a rational point, and its Jacobian
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the genus via Riemann–Roch for function fields and the divisor class group, which is the function-field avatar of the Jacobian; there is no Jacobian *variety* over ℚ, no abelian variety and no Mordell–Weil theorem for a higher-genus Jacobian.

targets.target: Coleman integrals and annihilating differentials; Frobenius continuation and rigid/de Rham cohomology
targets.note: Nothing towards p-adic integration exists: no rigid analytic spaces, no overconvergent or wide-open neighbourhoods, no Frobenius lift, no Monsky–Washnitzer or rigid cohomology (`grep -i 'Coleman|overconvergent|rigidAnalytic'` over both libraries is empty).

targets.target: Residue-disc zero bounds (Newton polygon / Strassmann bound on zeros of a p-adic power series in a disc)
targets.note: Absent. There is no p-adic power-series zero-counting result in either library, so the disc-by-disc bound the method turns on cannot be stated.

targets.target: Chabauty's theorem: for rank r < g the rational points are finite, with completeness of the enumeration
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

duplicates.note: L1 owns the Frobenius continuation, Coleman functions and the uniqueness principle that ED.4 consumes; the integration theory is stated in both.

targets.target: Finite reduction maps J(ℚ) → J(𝔽_p) and compatible residue conditions
targets.note: Good reduction of an elliptic curve is defined in Mathlib, but there is no reduction homomorphism on points of a Jacobian, no Jacobian, and no compatibility diagram of the kind the sieve needs.

targets.target: The sieve intersection and the proof that it eliminates all unlisted points
targets.note: Absent; the Mordell–Weil sieve appears nowhere in either library.

targets.target: Integral-point and hyperelliptic workflows with their covering maps
targets.note: No hyperelliptic curves and no coverings of curves with descent data are present.

targets.target: A combination certificate recording index/saturation assumptions, primes and images
targets.note: Depends on ED.3's saturation and ED.4's Chabauty bound, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Consumption of the quadratic/nonabelian Chabauty construction and implementation of its integration/precision certificates
targets.note: An integration layer over AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.5; neither the depth-two quotient nor the p-adic height equations exist in either library.

targets.target: Maintained worked Thue, S-unit, elliptic and higher-genus examples with proof-producing output
targets.note: Example maintenance and output plumbing over ED.2–ED.5, not new mathematics; none of the underlying methods is built.

targets.target: Advertised sufficient termination conditions per algorithm
targets.note: Documentation/bookkeeping about the algorithms of earlier layers.

duplicates.note: NC.5 owns the quadratic Chabauty construction, the p-adic height equations and the rank-versus-Picard-number criterion; ED.6 only consumes and packages them.

FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.summary: Nothing specific to Faltings' proof exists in either library. Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field (proper geometrically integral group schemes with commutative Hom groups, endomorphism rings, isogenies, products and base change), and has the elliptic-curve isogeny theory (degrees, kernels, deg(n·f) = n²·deg f, deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q)) and finite flat group schemes with Cartier duality; Mathlib supplies heights with Northcott for elements of a number field, Hermite's discriminant finiteness, class-group finiteness (the commutative rank-one case of Jordan–Zassenhaus), semisimple modules and elliptic-curve reduction types. Genuinely missing: polarisations, duals and moduli of abelian varieties, Tate modules, the Faltings height and its isogeny estimate, p-divisible groups and Néron models, Zarhin's trick, the general Jordan–Zassenhaus theorem, semisimplicity and Tate's isogeny theorem, Shafarevich finiteness, and the elliptic consequences (End_ℚ(E) = ℤ, finiteness of ℚ-isogeny classes and of prime isogeny degrees).

targets.target: Finiteness of polarised abelian varieties of bounded height over a fixed number field, with fixed dimension and polarisation degree
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field (with Hom groups, isogenies, products and base change) but no polarisations of them (its polarisations are of Hodge structures), no moduli and no heights of abelian varieties. The Northcott input the layer cites is in Mathlib only for elements of a fixed number field; the absolute height is defined with no API, and bounded-degree finiteness exists only as finiteness of integer polynomials of bounded degree and Mahler measure.

targets.target: Descent and level-structure arguments converting moduli points into isomorphism classes
targets.note: No moduli space of abelian varieties and no level structures exist in either library.

targets.target: Zarhin's trick (A⁴ × Â⁴ is principally polarised) and the resulting finiteness transfer
targets.note: There is no dual abelian variety and no polarisation, and `Zarhin` occurs nowhere in the sources.

targets.target: Jordan–Zassenhaus: finitely many isomorphism classes of lattices over an order in a semisimple ℚ-algebra
targets.note: Only the commutative rank-one case is available: finiteness of the class group of a ring of integers (and of integral closures in finite extensions), i.e. of the rank-one lattices over the maximal order of a number field up to isomorphism. Orders in noncommutative semisimple ℚ-algebras and finiteness of their lattice classes are absent from both libraries.

duplicates.note: R35.6 exports the bounded-height comparison and the product/polarisation identities for Northcott and Zarhin’s trick, the same height and Zarhin inputs R28.1 states.
R35.5 proves the moduli (theta) height comparison with the Faltings height that R28.1’s finiteness on moduli uses.
M6 compares isomorphism classes with rational moduli points through the descent obstruction and exports it to height finiteness, R28.1’s descent and level-structure target.

targets.target: The Faltings (stable) height of an abelian variety over a number field
targets.note: No Arakelov theory, hermitian Hodge line or arithmetic degree exists; `Faltings` and `Arakelov` occur in neither library's declarations.

targets.target: Faltings' isogeny-height estimate, including primes dividing the isogeny degree
targets.note: Absent together with its inputs: integral invariant differentials of Néron models, finite flat group schemes over rings of integers and p-divisible groups.

targets.target: Boundedness of the height within an isogeny class
targets.note: Absent; Northcott in Mathlib gives no height bound.

targets.target: p-divisible groups and the integral differential calculations behind the estimate
targets.note: No p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group, Néron model or Raynaud-type classification exists. Tau Ceti has finite locally free commutative affine group schemes over any ring with Cartier duality, and isogenies of abelian varieties over a field.

duplicates.note: R35.3 defines the stable Faltings height and its behaviour under extension, the height R28.2 estimates.
R11.6 supplies the semistable and good-reduction facts for the isogeny-height analysis of R28.

targets.target: Finiteness of isomorphism classes within an isogeny class over a fixed field, with the field-of-definition restriction
targets.note: Absent; it depends on R28.1 and R28.2, which have no library support.

targets.target: Eventual stationarity of h(A_n) along the isogeny tower (Faltings' 1984 erratum form)
targets.note: No Faltings height, hence no sequence of heights.

targets.target: The ℓ-divisible group formed by the tail of the tower of closure group schemes
targets.note: No ℓ-divisible groups and no scheme-theoretic closure of subgroup schemes in integral models exist.

targets.target: Companion finiteness statements for products and polarisations
targets.note: Products of abelian varieties exist in Tau Ceti; polarisations and the finiteness statements do not.

targets.target: Semisimplicity of the Galois representation V_ℓ(A)
targets.note: Semisimple modules and representations and Maschke's theorem for finite groups are in Mathlib, but no Tate module of an abelian variety or elliptic curve exists (Tau Ceti proves only #ker[n] = n² for elliptic curves over an algebraically closed field), so V_ℓ(A) cannot be formed.

targets.target: Tate's comparison Hom_F(A,B) ⊗ ℚ_ℓ ≅ Hom_{G_F}(V_ℓA, V_ℓB), with injectivity and surjectivity proved separately
targets.note: The left-hand Hom groups exist (Tau Ceti's commutative group of homomorphisms of abelian varieties, and for elliptic curves the isogeny Hom group with deg(n·f) = n²·deg f, which makes it torsion-free), but neither finite generation nor any Tate module exists.

targets.target: The isogeny criterion: isomorphic rational Tate modules imply isogenous abelian varieties
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti has the Frobenius trace of an elliptic curve over a finite field and deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q), but no characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on a Tate module and no isogeny criterion.

targets.target: Graph constructions and the semisimple endomorphism algebra (Poincaré reducibility) used in the argument
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the endomorphism ring of an abelian variety and, for elliptic curves, End without zero divisors; abelian subvarieties, Poincaré complete reducibility and semisimplicity of End⁰(A) are absent.

duplicates.note: A6 proves finite generation and torsion-freeness of Hom, the semisimple endomorphism algebra and Poincaré complete reducibility, the Hom-side inputs R28.4 states.
R01.6 constructs Tate modules of elliptic curves and abelian varieties with their Galois action, the V_ℓ(A) of R28.4.

targets.target: Shafarevich finiteness: finitely many abelian varieties of fixed dimension over F with good reduction outside a finite set S
targets.note: Absent. Hermite's theorem (finitely many number fields of bounded discriminant, with an explicit count in Tau Ceti) is the only finiteness theorem of this shape; even finiteness of number fields of given degree unramified outside S is not stated, and good reduction exists only for elliptic curves.

targets.target: The finite Frobenius-data or moduli-boundedness argument producing a height bound from good reduction
targets.note: Absent; neither the Frobenius data of abelian varieties nor a moduli height exists.

targets.target: The polarisation and semistable-extension reductions
targets.note: No polarisations, Néron models or semistable reduction theorem exist; Mathlib has minimal models and the good/multiplicative/additive trichotomy for elliptic curves, and Tau Ceti's stable-reduction files contain only the combinatorics of numerical types.

duplicates.note: RP.4 applies Shafarevich finiteness after a Parshin covering; both layers turn on the same finiteness theorem.
R25.4 proves nonexistence of semistable abelian varieties over ℚ with good reduction outside one small prime, a sharp special case of the same good-reduction finiteness.

targets.target: Export of semisimplicity, the rational Hom comparison and isogeny detection to the elliptic-curve and abelian-variety types
targets.note: An interface over R28.4–R28.5, none of whose results exist; the target types exist.

targets.target: Finiteness of the ℚ-isomorphism classes in the ℚ-isogeny class of an elliptic curve
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves isogeny kernels finite and degrees multiplicative; finiteness of the isogeny class is not proved.

targets.target: Finite generation of Hom_ℚ(E,E′) and its rank one when End_ℚ(E) = ℤ
targets.note: Hom is an abelian group with deg(n·f) = n²·deg f, so torsion-freeness is immediate, but finite generation, End_ℚ(E) = ℤ and the rank-one statement are not proved.

targets.target: Finitely many prime degrees of rational isogenies
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: R29.1 proves End_ℚ(E) = ℤ, rank one of Hom_ℚ(E,E′) and finiteness of prime isogeny degrees from Faltings, the same consequences R28.6 exports.
A6 proves finite generation of Hom groups, which R28.6 restates for elliptic curves.
